title: Dela Rosa's office acknowledges complaint on prolonged absence, assures Senate commitment
summary: The office of Sen. Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa has formally acknowledge the receipt of the notice of complaint filed regarding his prolonged absence and assures his commitment to the Senate as an…

blocks.text: The office of Sen. Ronald "Bato" dela Rosa has formally acknowledge the receipt of the notice of complaint filed regarding his prolonged absence and assures his commitment to the Senate as an institution.

In a letter dated November 19, 2026 addressed to Senate Committee on Ethics and Privileges chair Sen. Vicente "Tito" Sotto III, Dela Rosa's chief of staff Marianne Kristel Dela Rosa-Estoesta said the said notice they received was dated November 5 on the complaint filed by Wag Kang KuCorrupt.

"For the record, the transmittal received by this Office contains exclusively of the main complaint and the five (5) affidavits executed by Susan Villanueva, Jasmine Ong, Cielo Magno, Jaimee Baliton, and Christopher Cabahaug," Dela Rosa-Estoesta said.

She also asked, in order to their records are complete and to prepare, if there are more affidavits that are to be expected as there were nine signatories to the original complaint that was filed last February 2026.
"Rest assured that Senator Dela Rosa remains steadfast in his commitment to the Senate as an institution and to the processes of the Committee of Ethics and Privileges," said Dela Rosa-Estoesta.
This refers to the letter transmitted by the Senate Committee to Senator Dela Rosa about the complaint lodged against him due to his prolonged absence.

The Wag Kang KuCorrupt group on Friday, November 20, 2026, posted the panel's transmittal letter to Dela Rosa on Facebook. Committee chair Senator Tito Sotto, who signed the document dated October 22, 2026, later confirmed the complaint to reporters.
The group's petition reasoned that Dela Rosa's prolonged absence showed a dereliction of duty and a grave abuse of privilege.

"Under ordinary working conditions in both the public and private sectors, employees who fail to report for work without authorized leave are ordinarily subjected to disciplinary measures, including salary deductions, suspension, or even outright termination. Breadwinners across the country work tirelessly, often under difficult conditions, precisely because their families' welfare depends on daily accountability and performance," the group's original complaint read.
The ethics panel gave Dela Rosa 15 days upon receipt of the complaint to provide his written response and any information regarding the matter.

Senator Sotto, in reply to the question of Dela Rosa's office on whether there are more affidavits related to the filed complaint, said "no other submission has been made in relation to the complaint apart from those transmitted to you under the Committee letter dated October 22, 2026."

"The Committee reiterates that you submit a written response, together with any information related to the complaint, within the period stated in the said letter, pursuant to Section 18 (C) of the rules of the Senate Committee Ethics and Privileges," Sotto added.
Dela Rosa started missing Senate engagements in 2025 following reports that the International Criminal Court (ICC) had issued an arrest warrant against him.

He resurfaced on May 11, but left Senate custody in the early morning of May 14 after a shooting incident erupted inside the legislative chamber's premises. He has not been seen publicly ever since, and now faces a P50-million bounty for information leading to his arrest. — BAP, GMA News
